cues.zh: 就像我们说院子里放着些木柴。
cues.en: Talking about like that like we had some wood out in the yard.

cues.zh: 不说“把它搬进屋”，你会说“把它扛进屋”，就像
cues.en: Instead of saying "carry it in the house" you'd say "tote it in the house" and like

cues.zh: 如果你有东西想装进纸袋，你会装进纸“兜”里
cues.en: if you had something that you wanted to put in a paper bag, you'd put in a paper "poke"

cues.zh: 你知道，而不是纸袋。
cues.en: you know instead of a paper bag.

cues.zh: 嗯，这地方的人说话的方式，我猜更像是你们说的乡下人
cues.en: Well, the way people talk around here, I guess it'd be what more like you'd call hillbilly

cues.zh: 风格之类的吧，我猜，我也不清楚。
cues.en: style or something, I guess, I don't know.

cues.zh: 这就是山地话。
cues.en: It's just Mountain Talk.

cues.zh: 你们本地人大多说山地话。
cues.en: Most of your local people have your Mountain Talk.

cues.zh: 这样你就能分辨山里人和外地人，
cues.en: That's the way you can tell the mountain people from your outsiders,

cues.zh: 凭他们说的语言。
cues.en: by their language they use.

cues.zh: 比如说，“我在那边见你。”
cues.en: Say, "I'll see ya over yonder."

cues.zh: 意思是像在韦恩斯维尔见你。
cues.en: That means I'll see you like in Waynesville.

cues.zh: 有点像山地话。
cues.en: It's a Mountain Talk, kinda.

cues.zh: 从不停歇，就像在唱歌一样，你知道的。
cues.en: Never nothing stops, it's like a-singin', you know.

cues.zh: 我们就像在唱歌一样。
cues.en: We're kinda like we're singing.

cues.zh: Lida说我们是在唱歌，不是说话。
cues.en: Lida said we're singing, not talking.

cues.zh: 是啊，我喜欢我的轻便摩托。
cues.en: Ya, I like my moped.

cues.zh: 大家都听说过Graham County，对吧？
cues.en: Everybody hears about Graham County, don't they?

cues.zh: 那儿的人有多好，多愿意帮你。
cues.en: How good the people is, how they'll help you.

cues.zh: 我会遇到素不相识、这辈子从没见过的人，而我也会尽力帮他们
cues.en: I run into people I don't know, never seen them in my life, and I help them in any way

cues.zh: 能帮多少帮多少。
cues.en: I can.

cues.zh: 有人说，总有一天你会被人敲脑袋，我说：“那要是真被敲了，敲就敲呗。”
cues.en: Somebody said, one day you'll get knocked in the head, I said, "well, if I do, I'm just knocked."

cues.zh: 我们就是心地善良。
cues.en: We're just good-hearted.

cues.zh: 你遇到的每个人，99%都是这样。
cues.en: Everybody you meet, just 99% of them.

cues.zh: 如果我不是住在这儿，我会搬过来，你不也会吗？
cues.en: If I didn't live here, I'd move, wouldn't you?

cues.zh: 你能去哪儿度假呢？
cues.en: Where you gonna go on vacation?

cues.zh: 要是我去度假，我就待在这附近。
cues.en: If I was gonna go on vacation I'd just stay right around here.

cues.zh: 反正一直待在这儿也不介意。
cues.en: Wouldn't mind this all the time anyhow.

cues.zh: 我们比整个国家落后20年。
cues.en: We are 20 years behind the whole country.

cues.zh: 但我不会跟任何人换地方。
cues.en: But I wouldn't swap places with nobody.

cues.zh: 待在这儿比别人落后20年，我心里舒服多了，总比搬到
cues.en: I feel much more comfortable here being 20 years behind everybody than I would be a-settlin'

cues.zh: 好多地方去、过得那么痛苦强。
cues.en: a lot of places and being so miserable.

cues.zh: 你不喜欢你的邻居，你不跟邻居说话，你对整个世界都心怀怨恨。
cues.en: You don't like your neighbor, you don't speak to your neighbor, you're bitter with the world.

cues.zh: 亚特兰大就是个好例子。
cues.en: Atlanta's a good example.

cues.zh: 或者罗利。
cues.en: Or Raleigh.

cues.zh: 你开车沿街走，每个人都敞开心扉，按着喇叭，谁也不认识
cues.en: You drive down the street and everybody's wide open, blowing their horns and don't know

cues.zh: 谁也不认识，也不想认识谁，更不关心谁。
cues.en: nobody and don't want to know nobody and don't care about nobody.

cues.zh: 这里就大不一样了。
cues.en: It's quite a bit different up here.

cues.zh: 嗯，我在华盛顿特区住过大约四年半，我宁愿去地狱
cues.en: Well I Iived in Washington, D.C. about four and a half years and I'd just as soon be in hell

cues.zh: 摔断脊背，也不愿住在那儿。
cues.en: with my back broke than live there.

cues.zh: 这里的人彼此之间太好了。
cues.en: People are so good to each other here.

cues.zh: 山地话里的许多词语和表达对外人来说很陌生。
cues.en: Many of the words and expressions in Mountain Speech are unfamiliar to outsiders.

cues.zh: 苏格兰-爱尔兰移民从欧洲带来了大部分词汇，但许多新词和新表达
cues.en: Scots Irish settlers brought much of the vocabulary from Europe, but many new words and expressions

cues.zh: 是他们的后代在这里发明的。
cues.en: were invented here by their descendants.

cues.zh: 意思就是有人造出了一个奇怪的词。
cues.en: There's just somebody coming up with a strange word is what it means.

cues.zh: 比如说你想做成某件事，你在做某个东西。
cues.en: I mean let's say you're trying to get something done, you're building something.

cues.zh: 然后你一看，就像 sigogglin 这个词。
cues.en: And you'll take a look at it, like the word sigogglin.

cues.zh: 你看着它，全都歪歪扭扭的，你可能就造出个词叫“sigogglin”。
cues.en: You're looking at it and it's all out of line and you might just come up with a word "sigogglin".

cues.zh: 我自己也这么干。
cues.en: I do that myself.

cues.zh: 一时想不出来，但我自己造了不少新词，所以你
cues.en: Can't think of anything right off, but I come up with a lot of new words myself and so you

cues.zh: 旁边站着的人听到了，好吧，这就叫 sigogglin。
cues.en: get somebody standing around, they hear that and okay it's sigogglin.

cues.zh: 比如木匠活儿干得很差，你就说这全是 sigogglin。
cues.en: Say a carpenter's done a real poor job and then you say that's all sigogglin.

cues.zh: 你知道，他墙没砌直，或者
cues.en: You know, he didn't have his walls straight or

cues.zh: 他们退后一看，有什么东西歪着，就会说：“那玩意儿 sigogglin。”
cues.en: They'd stand back and look with something angled like, they'd say, "That thing's sigogglin"

cues.zh: 他们会说：“我想让你看看。”
cues.en: They'd say, "I want you to look."

cues.zh: 我会说，“这是什么？”
cues.en: I'd say, "What is it?"

cues.zh: 如果你在建造某种东西，那边那个就是歪的。
cues.en: If you're building some kind of, so that's sigogglin right yonder.

cues.zh: 所以那条往上走的老路，说那东西是歪的。
cues.en: And so that old road going up there, say that thing's sigogglin.

cues.zh: 我祖母，她总是说人很壮实。
cues.en: My grandmother, she's always talking about people being stout.

cues.zh: 或者说瘦长。
cues.en: Or gaint.

cues.zh: 她会用像“peckerwood”这样的词。
cues.en: She used words like "peckerwood".

cues.zh: 如果是她不喜欢的人，她会叫他peckerwood。
cues.en: If it's somebody she didn't like, she'd call him a peckerwood.

cues.zh: 如果是她不认识但可能还不错的人，她对他没有敌意
cues.en: If it's somebody she didn't know but he's probably alright, she didn't have any animosity

cues.zh: 她会说，“他是个jasper。”
cues.en: for him, she'd say, "He is a jasper."

cues.zh: “今天早上有个jasper来这儿敲了门，”你知道的。
cues.en: "There's this jasper come by here this morning and knocked on the door," you know.

cues.zh: 但如果是推销员，“门外走廊上有个peckerwood。”
cues.en: But if it was a salesman, "There's this peckerwood out there on the porch."

cues.zh: 就像人们以前，你知道的，比如你去商店，说“把它装袋子里”？
cues.en: It's like people used to, you know, like you go in a store, say "put it in the bag"?

cues.zh: 老年人说把它装进纸袋里。
cues.en: Old people says you put in a poke.

cues.zh: 那是个袋子。
cues.en: That's a bag.

cues.zh: 小时候，我常去商店，走两英里去店里，然后扛着一袋25
cues.en: I used to go to the store, walk two miles, the store, when I was a kid and carry a 25

cues.zh: 磅重的面粉回家。
cues.en: pound poke of flour home.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，是“面粉”（flour），不是“花儿”（fler）。
cues.en: That's "fler", by the way, not "flour".

cues.zh: 我和我的两个姐妹、一个兄弟，会在家里等着他们带糖果回来。
cues.en: And me and my two sisters, one brother, we'd be a-waiting on them at the house to get our candy.

cues.zh: 索尔，我之前提到的那个年长的人，有一小袋糖果。
cues.en: Saul, the older man I was talking about, had a little poke of candy.

cues.zh: 他说：“哎呀，我忘记买什么东西了！”
cues.en: He said, "Well I forgot to get anything!"

cues.zh: 但我们会尖叫！
cues.en: But we'd scream!

cues.zh: “哦，在这儿呢！”
cues.en: "Oh here it is!"

cues.zh: “Plumb”是我成长过程中常用的词。
cues.en: "Plumb" was a common word when I was growing up.

cues.zh: 这个也plumb，那个也plumb，你会说“plumb over there”（就在那边）。
cues.en: Plumb this and plumb that and you'd get "plumb over there."

cues.zh: “哎，他真是plumb wore out（彻底累坏了）。”
cues.en: "Well, he was just plumb wore out."

cues.zh: 还有那个铜矿，那条矿脉，他们从地下挖隧道，一直通到这里的Snowbird。
cues.en: And that copper mine, that vein, they tunneled under the ground plumb out through here to Snowbird.

cues.zh: 就像风在吹。
cues.en: Like the wind was a-blowing.

cues.zh: 你知道的，很多空气。
cues.en: You know, a lot of air.

cues.zh: 他们会说外面很airish（通风、有风）。
cues.en: They'd say it's very airish outside.

cues.zh: Airish？
cues.en: Airish?

cues.zh: 意思是外面有点冷。
cues.en: It means it's a little bit chilly outside.

cues.zh: 意思是，airish，就是说今天有点凉。
cues.en: It means, it's airish, it means it's chilly today.

cues.zh: 就现在，我们说话的这会儿，今天挺凉的。
cues.en: It's airish today right now as we speak.

cues.zh: 风吹着，微风阵阵。
cues.en: The air is blowing and breezy.

cues.zh: 好东西，你知道好东西吗，你去店里买瓶可乐？
cues.en: A good one, you know a good one, you'd go to the store and buy a coke?

cues.zh: 那时候他们管这叫dopes。
cues.en: They'd call them dopes back then.

cues.zh: 我不知道你有没有听谁这么说过。
cues.en: I don't know if you'd ever hear anybody say that or not.

cues.zh: 那是我小时候喝的东西，叫，他们有Nehi，有Pepsi-Cola，
cues.en: That's what we drank when I was a kid and it was called, they had Nehi, they had Pepsi-Cola,

cues.zh: Royal Crown Cola，好多呢，那都叫dope。
cues.en: Royal Crown Cola, a lot of them, that was dope.

cues.zh: 哦，dope！
cues.en: Oh, a dope!

cues.zh: 你说的是汽水、苏打水那种，对。
cues.en: You're talking about like a soda pop, soda water, yeah.

cues.zh: 对，苏打水，对。
cues.en: Yeah, soda water, yeah.

cues.zh: Dope。
cues.en: Dope.

cues.zh: 小时候这附近的人都这么叫。
cues.en: That's all they ever call them around here as a kid.

cues.zh: 现在你要是往Ernestine家那边上去，
cues.en: Now if you go up toward Ernestine's place up there,

cues.zh: 在快到Tony家拐弯那一段，那片松树林边上，对，就沿着
cues.en: Stop along there about where you turn up to Tony's there in them pine patch, right, along with

cues.zh: 那座木屋，你大概能在那儿看到一只袋鼠。
cues.en: that log house, you'll probably see a boomer right there.

cues.zh: 一位女士走过来说：“哦”，我说：“那是只不错的boomer。”
cues.en: A lady came through and she said, "Oh," I said, "that's a pretty boomer."

cues.zh: 她说：“Boomer？什么是boomer？”
cues.en: She said, "A boomer? What's a boomer?"

cues.zh: 你知道boomer是什么，对吧？
cues.en: You know what a boomer is, don't you?

cues.zh: 你见过吗？
cues.en: You ever see one?

cues.zh: 什么是boomer？
cues.en: What's a boomer?

cues.zh: 它们会发出很多叽叽喳喳的声音，大概有码头老鼠那么大。
cues.en: They make a lot of chatting noises, they're about the size of a wharf rat.

cues.zh: 码头老鼠？
cues.en: A wharf rat?

cues.zh: 对，码头老鼠。
cues.en: Yeah, a wharf rat.

cues.zh: 大个的老鼠。
cues.en: Big old rat.

cues.zh: Boomer就像小松鼠。
cues.en: A boomer is like a little squirrel.

cues.zh: 它不是松鼠。
cues.en: It's not a squirrel.

cues.zh: 它是灰松鼠和花栗鼠的混合。
cues.en: It's a mix between a grey squirrel and a chipmunk.

cues.zh: 只不过它是红色的。
cues.en: Except it's red.

cues.zh: 能吃吗？
cues.en: Can you eat them?

cues.zh: 能。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 她说：“那是红松鼠。”
cues.en: She said, "That's a red squirrel."

cues.zh: 我说：“嗯，对我来说那就是boomer。”
cues.en: I said, "Well, to me that's a boomer."

cues.zh: 我们一直叫它boomer。
cues.en: We always called it boomers.

cues.zh: 比如说那是片老scald。
cues.en: Say it's an old scald.

cues.zh: 意思是那是块老旧死地，什么都长不出来，懂吧？
cues.en: That mean that's old dead land, won't grow nothing, you know?

cues.zh: 我们叫它scald。
cues.en: We call it scald.

cues.zh: 我不知道你们有没有人听过这个说法，我知道你们听过。
cues.en: I don't know if any of you ever heard that, or I know you have.

cues.zh: 这叫烫伤，贫瘠的土地。
cues.en: Call it a scald, poor land.

cues.zh: 就像我货车里的化油器，全被那些陈年脏东西堵住了。
cues.en: That's like the carburetor in my van, all gaumed up with all that old dirty stuff.

cues.zh: 堵住了。
cues.en: Gaum.

cues.zh: 意思是乱糟糟的。
cues.en: It means like all cluttered up.

cues.zh: 堵住了。
cues.en: Gaumed up.

cues.zh: 对，就是说一团糟。
cues.en: Yeah, that means it's in a mess.

cues.zh: 我也会这么说。
cues.en: That's what I would've said.

cues.zh: 他们不知道自己是在跟这么有学问的人说话，对吧？
cues.en: They didn't know they were talking to such educated folks, did they?

cues.zh: 不说“那边”，你知道，“在那边”，而是说“在那半边”。
cues.en: Instead of saying yonder, you know, "over yonder," it's "over yander."

cues.zh: 你听过这个词吗？
cues.en: Do you ever hear that word?

cues.zh: 在那半边？
cues.en: Over yander?

cues.zh: 对，我就说在那半边。没错。
cues.en: Yeah, well I say over yander. Yeah.

cues.zh: 我小时候，我妈会走到我们跟前说，
cues.en: My momma used to come up to use when we was little and she'd say,

cues.zh: “鹅？还是公鹅？”她会揪着两只耳朵。
cues.en: "Goose? Or gander?" She'd pull each ear.

cues.zh: 你要是说鹅，她就说往这边揪，松的。
cues.en: If you say goose, she'd say pull it here, loose.

cues.zh: 说公鹅，她就往那半边揪得老远。
cues.en: And say gander, she'd pull it way over yander.

cues.zh: 他们都认识我。
cues.en: They all know me.

cues.zh: 他们会说，那半边来的，骑着他的哈雷摩托。
cues.en: They'd say yander comes him a-riding that Harley-Davidson.

cues.zh: 他们以为那是哈雷摩托。
cues.en: They think it's a Harley.
